prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-02-24. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 0.63 |
| Retained earnings       | -5,086M |
| Current liabilities     | 3,973M |
| Current assets          | 2,495M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 3,652M |
| Total liabilities       | 52,835M |
| Total assets            | 63,190M |
| EBIT / operating income | 1,161M |
| Revenue                 | 2,738M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-02-24, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The reported current ratio of 0.63 signals acute liquidity pressure, while negative retained earnings of -5,086 M combined with total liabilities of 52,835 M versus equity of only 3,652 M indicate a deeply impaired balance sheet and high leverage. Although positive EBIT provides some offset, the overall profile is consistent with substantial default risk but not an immediate payment default.
DECISION: CCC
(The data are also consistent with CCC+ or CCC- given the single-period snapshot.)
